findings.finding: The repository describes an ASIN as a "10-character" identifier in 75 places. Amazon's own link-format help says "ASIN is the 10-digit code that Amazon uses to denote specific products", and real ASINs such as B0CDY277D3 contain letters, so "10-character" is the functionally accurate reading but not the published wording.
findings.impact: No factual conclusion changes: both readings agree the supplied 9-character tokens cannot be ASINs. The risk is one of sourcing style, in a project whose claim is verbatim quotation: a reviewer checking the quote against the source will not find "10-character" on it.
findings.recommendation: Where the sentence cites S24, quote "10-digit" and add the observed 10-character form as this repository's own note, rather than paraphrasing inside the quotation.
findings.owner_note: Not fixed in this task: the 75 occurrences sit in other sessions' ledgers, pages and docs.

findings.finding: Disclosure placement is inconsistent across the marketing namespace. Measured 2026-11-15: 7 pages carry an outbound amazon.com/dp/ affiliate anchor (27 anchors), but only the 3 product articles carry the in-context "(paid link)" label. The four without it are marketing/articles/index.html, comparison.html, flagged.html and verification.html.
findings.impact: The page-level Amazon disclosure required by the Operating Agreement is present on every page, so this is not a breach of that requirement. It diverges from US FTC placement guidance and from the repository's own article template, which renders the marker.
findings.recommendation: Extend the in-context marker to the four pages that lack it and assert it in the marketing gate, so the label cannot silently disappear again.
findings.owner_note: Logged for the owner; not implemented here because it touches another session's generator.

findings.finding: This task's own first version of its disclosure proposal asserted that no page carried the "(paid link)" marker. That was wrong: the grep covered marketing/*.html and missed the marketing/articles/ subdirectory.
findings.impact: None surviving. The claim was re-measured with a recursive count before publication and corrected in place, with the correction stated rather than silently overwritten.
findings.recommendation: Kept on the record on purpose. A review surface that hides its own first error gives a reader less reason to trust the rest of it, not more.
findings.owner_note: No action required; published so the correction stays auditable.
